study type: Case study, in vitro cell study, animal model study (mouse)
exposure: Compound heterozygous variants in MMP-9 (c.59C > T, p.A20V and c.493G > A, p.D165N)
MMP-9 inhibition (genetic, biologic, or pharmacologic in mice)
outcome: Significantly less Activin A production (by macrophages expressing MMP-9 variants)
Abrogation of trauma-induced HO (in FOP mouse models)
Sequestration of Activin A in the extracellular matrix (ECM)
cohort: A 35-year-old man with the pathogenic ACVR1R206H variant of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) displaying extreme resilience, compared to healthy controls and individuals with quiescent FOP for plasma biomarkers, as well as human proinflammatory M1-like macrophages and multiple FOP mouse models.
finding: A 35-year-old man with FOP exhibited extreme resilience to heterotopic ossification (HO) due to naturally occurring compound heterozygous MMP-9 variants, which was further shown in cell and mouse models where MMP-9 inhibition abrogated trauma-induced HO by sequestering Activin A, identifying MMP-9 as a critical druggable target in FOP pathogenesis.
